<STRUCT_0001>
To arrive at the correct converse of this lemma we ask
whether given a relatively ample
invertible sheaf <MATH_0001> there exists an integer <MATH_0002> such
that <MATH_0003> is relatively very ample? In general this
is false. There are several things that prevent this from being true:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> Even if <MATH_0004> is affine, it can happen that no finite integer
<MATH_0005> works because <MATH_0006> is not of finite type, see
Example <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0004> The base not being quasi-compact means the result can be
prevented from being true even with <MATH_0007> finite type. Namely, given
a field <MATH_0008> there exists a scheme <MATH_0009> of finite type over <MATH_0010> with
an ample invertible sheaf <MATH_0011> so that the smallest
tensor power of <MATH_0012> which is very ample is the <MATH_0013>th
power. See Example <REF_0002>.
Taking <MATH_0014> to be the disjoint union of the schemes <MATH_0015> mapping
to the disjoint union of copies of <MATH_0016> gives an example.
<STRUCT_0005>
To see our version of the converse take a look at
Lemma <REF_0003> below.
We will do some preliminary work before proving it.
